stances_toward.note: Lithuania is Belarus's sharpest neighbour: it hosted Tsikhanouskaya's office since 2020, closed Klaipeda to Belarusian potash, is the veto-holder on the EU potash question (Budrys, 26 May 2026) and was the target of the smuggling balloons that shut Vilnius airport (Oct 2025, Jan and Apr 2026). It closed its last two crossings on 27-29 Oct 2025 until 20 Nov, and Minsk answered by holding Lithuanian trucks (about 200 still detained in May 2026) and by a EUR 12bn arbitration claim. Cooling, not adversary: the crossings reopened, Washington is pressing for better Belarus-Lithuania ties (Coale, Mar 2026) and Vilnius is divided on easing (47/46 in an LRT poll). No source uses the word 'rival': our reading (confidence C). Bond - grievance: sanctions on potash and the exile base.

relations_to.summary: Before the 2022 shutdown Belarusian potash made up a third of Klaipeda port's turnover at its peak and Belaruskali held 30% of its bulk terminal; Lithuania closed the transit route, Belarusian potash moved to Ust-Luga and St Petersburg, and Belaruskali claims EUR 12bn in arbitration (decision not expected before 2027).

sources.title: Belarus, the EU and fertilizers: what happens when sanctions stop working

relations_to.summary: Smuggling balloons from Belarus closed Vilnius airport repeatedly in Oct 2025; Lithuania closed its last two crossings (Salcininkai, Medininkai) on 27-29 Oct and reopened them on 20 Nov 2025; more balloons on 27-28 Jan and 9-10 Apr 2026 brought protest notes and threats to close again.

sources.title: Lithuania closes its border with Belarus for a month
Lithuania to close border with Belarus over smuggling balloon threat, with some exemptions

relations_to.summary: Belarus retaliated against Lithuanian haulage: trucks with Lithuanian plates were blocked from leaving Belarus after the Oct 2025 closure (estimates from about 280 to over 1,000 trucks); up to 200 were still detained in May 2026, some perhaps never to be returned because storage fees exceed their value.
